doc: When a request that carried a picture fails, only a RELIABLE structured signal may turn that into 'this model does not take images' (and so into a text-only fallback). The signal is the provider's own error code or type (error.code, error.type, or the same two keys at the top level), compared case-insensitively against `codes`, on an HTTP 400, 415 or 422 only. A status alone proves nothing (404 may be a wrong model name, 413 is a payload that is too large, 400/422 may be a schema mistake), a human-readable message is never trusted, and auth statuses never count. The body is parsed into one local boolean and thrown away: no part of it is stored or shown. No signal = the failure is real and propagates (fail closed).

cases.name: 422 with a top-level code, any case
a message that says so is not a signal
cases.body: {"error":{"message":"image input is not supported by this model"}}
